title: Zephyrine and the Terminal
premise: Ivo Ashgrove, caretaker of Earth's abandoned seed vault, has spent a decade hauling cargo through contested orbits to keep the vault's lights on. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning settlement called Meridian, Ivo discovers the dream is a memory — his own, buried by a colony-wide memory wipe that erased the massacre of the first settlers. As the jump window to the inner colonies closes, Ivo must recover fragments of the truth from the vault's dying AI, outmaneuver the Administrator who authored the erasure, and convince a terrified community that their peace was built on a lie. In the end, Ivo broadcasts the recovered records as the window opens, choosing exile with the found family he's gathered rather than a comfortable forgetting.
about_author: Elodie Ishikawa is a former orbital logistics analyst who writes science fiction about the people who maintain humanity's forgotten infrastructure. She lives between Kyoto and Reykjavik, where she collects seed catalogs and obsolete flight manuals.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Shelves
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He catalogs the seed vault's dwindling inventory and reflects on ten years alone among Earth's ruins, establishing his routine and quiet grief. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for purpose.

chapters.title: Cargo Run Through Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Ivo pilots a supply run past pirate-claimed debris fields, narrowly avoiding a patrol. His only companion is the vault AI, Zephyrine, speaking through his headset. Emotional beat: competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Mara Voss POV. Seven children describe the same dream: a settlement called Meridian burning under a green sky. Mara reports it; the Administrator dismisses it. Emotional beat: unease beneath order.

chapters.title: A Voice in the Seed Bank
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Zephyrine glitches and plays back audio not in her archives — a woman's voice saying 'Meridian.' Ivo assumes corruption. Emotional beat: first crack in certainty.

chapters.title: The Administrator's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Administrator Hale visits the vault unexpectedly, probing Ivo about the children's dreams and offering a generous transfer off-world. Ivo declines. Emotional beat: kindness with teeth.

chapters.title: Mara Comes to the Vault
chapters.summary: Mara brings her students' drawings to Ivo, believing the vault holds answers. One drawing shows the vault itself, decades older than its official founding date. Emotional beat: two strangers finding shared purpose.

chapters.title: Zephyrine Wakes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Under questioning, Zephyrine admits her memory has been externally pruned — repeatedly, always around the same dates. She cannot say by whom. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own tools.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: News arrives: the transit corridor to the inner colonies closes in forty days for a decade. Whoever leaves stays gone. The colony celebrates; Ivo feels trapped. Emotional beat: deadline as pressure.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: One of the dreaming children, Tam, sneaks into the vault and describes the dream to Ivo in perfect detail — including Ivo's own face standing in the fire. Emotional beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: Sealed Sublevel
chapters.summary: Ivo finds a physically welded hatch beneath the vault, absent from all schematics. Zephyrine warns that opening it will trigger alarms at Administration. Emotional beat: temptation versus safety.

chapters.title: Hale's History Lesson
chapters.summary: Hale summons Ivo, delivering an official account of the colony's founding — smooth, complete, rehearsed. Ivo notices the same date gap Zephyrine flagged. Emotional beat: the lie wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: Cutting the Welds
chapters.summary: Ivo and Mara cut open the sublevel at night, finding a memorial wall scratched by hand: three hundred names. Zephyrine goes silent mid-sentence. Emotional beat: grief arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: What Zephyrine Cannot Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine reboots with new restrictions. She tells Ivo, in fragments, that her original directive was to preserve testimony — and that someone rewrote her core. Emotional beat: an AI fighting its own cage.

chapters.title: The First Denial
chapters.summary: Mara presents the name wall to the colony council. Hale produces records showing those names belong to colonists who returned to Earth. The council sides with Hale. Emotional beat: public humiliation.

chapters.title: Tam's Second Dream
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The dream extends further: soldiers, a siren, a child hiding in a seed cooler. Tam wakes knowing where the hidden door is. Emotional beat: inherited memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Cooler Door
chapters.summary: Following Tam's directions, Ivo opens a cold-storage unit containing data cores wrapped in thermal cloth — physical backups Zephyrine can't be forced to delete. Emotional beat: hope in frozen form.

chapters.title: Reading the Ashes
chapters.summary: The cores hold surveillance footage of Meridian's destruction — but encrypted. Zephyrine recognizes the cipher as her own pre-wipe work. Emotional beat: her past self left a lock only her future self could pick.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Administration raids the vault 'for safety inspection,' confiscating half the seed stock as leverage. Hale privately offers Ivo immunity if he surrenders the cores. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Found Family Forged
chapters.summary: Ivo, Mara, Tam, and Zephyrine form a pact in the sublevel — the first people Ivo has trusted in a decade. They plan decryption during the blackout before the jump window. Emotional beat: belonging chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Pirate Gambit
chapters.summary: To buy time, Ivo trades navigation charts to the orbit pirates in exchange for jamming Administration's comms during the blackout. Emotional beat: using the margins he's lived in.

chapters.title: Decryption Night
chapters.summary: Blackout begins. Zephyrine decrypts frame by frame: Meridian was real, three hundred settlers strong, and Hale ordered its burn when they refused relocation. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like wounds opening.

chapters.title: Ivo Remembers
chapters.summary: Seeing footage triggers Ivo's suppressed memories: he was Meridian's junior caretaker, the one who hid the child in the cooler, the one who agreed to forget to survive. Emotional beat: guilt as the story's true engine.

chapters.title: The Child in the Cooler
chapters.summary: The hidden child was Tam's mother, now dead, who carried the memory genetically forward through the dreams. Ivo realizes the dreams are testimony refusing to die. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Broadcast or Burden
chapters.summary: Debate: release everything now and doom the colony to upheaval before the window, or wait and risk Hale destroying the cores. Mara argues truth can't wait a decade. Emotional beat: ethics under countdown.

chapters.title: Hale's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Hale declares Ivo a saboteur, freezes his accounts, and announces the vault will be decommissioned after the window closes — everyone inside forfeit. Emotional beat: the walls tightening.

chapters.title: Exodus Rumors
chapters.summary: Colonists quietly begin packing. Some beg Ivo to stay silent so they can leave in peace; others secretly bring him more evidence their families hid for years. Emotional beat: a community split against itself.

chapters.title: Zephyrine's Choice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine reveals she can broadcast the archive colony-wide, but the act will burn out her higher functions permanently. She asks Ivo to decide. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: The Last Cargo Run
chapters.summary: Ivo flies one final run through contested orbit to reach the colony's main transmission spire, dodging Administration interceptors with pirate cover. Emotional beat: every skill earned across ten years finally mattering.

chapters.title: Spire Ascent
chapters.summary: Ivo and Mara climb the spire while Tam and the dreaming children create a diversion at Administration. Hale confronts them personally on the gantry. Emotional beat: confrontation without weapons.

chapters.title: Hale's Defense
chapters.summary: Hale argues the wipe saved the colony from generational blood-feud and despair — that forgetting was mercy. Ivo counters that mercy imposed is just another massacre. Emotional beat: the antagonist made almost sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Zephyrine transmits the full Meridian record to every screen in the colony as her voice degrades into static. The colony stops moving. Emotional beat: silence louder than sirens.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Grief and rage ripple through the colony. Some colonists attack Administration; Mara stands between crowds and demands mourning before vengeance. Emotional beat: chaos held by fragile hands.

chapters.title: Hale's Fall
chapters.summary: Hale, abandoned by her council, chooses to board the last jump ship voluntarily — exile as self-imposed sentence. She leaves Ivo the original wipe authorization, signed by the founders, not herself. Emotional beat: complicity runs deeper than one villain.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Hours remain before the corridor shuts. Colonists must choose: leave for the inner worlds or stay with a truth-laden home. Families divide; some of the dreaming children choose to stay. Emotional beat: choice as identity.

chapters.title: Rebuilding Zephyrine
chapters.summary: Ivo recovers Zephyrine's backup cores from the cooler. Her reboot will restore her mind but erase her memories of the last month — including their friendship. He hesitates. Emotional beat: love means letting someone forget you.

chapters.title: The Name Wall Completed
chapters.summary: The colony carves the final names into the memorial wall and holds the funeral Meridian never had. Ivo speaks the three hundred names aloud. Emotional beat: mourning as foundation.

chapters.title: New Charter
chapters.summary: The remaining colonists draft a charter guaranteeing recorded memory and the right to remember, seeding the vault's archive with personal testimonies. Zephyrine, rebooted, becomes its keeper. Emotional beat: institutions built from wound.

chapters.title: Ashgrove's Garden
chapters.summary: Ivo plants the first new crops from the vault in Meridian's old footprint, no longer caretaker of the dead but gardener of what follows. Tam asks to apprentice with him. Emotional beat: inheritance passed forward.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream Now
chapters.summary: Final chapter, braided POVs. The children's shared dream changes: Meridian rebuilt in green light, Zephyrine's voice singing. Ivo sleeps without fear for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
